EQT AB ( EQT +4.05% ▲ ) just unveiled an announcement.

EQT AB reported strong momentum in the third quarter of 2026, underpinned by the completion of its combination with Coller Capital, now operating as Coller EQT, and an agreement to acquire Stockbridge, a leading U.S. real estate investment manager with about $17 billion in fee-generating assets. The group also launched a Middle East platform with a new Abu Dhabi office and introduced Nexus Asia, an Asia Pacific-focused evergreen strategy for private wealth clients, reinforcing its push into new regions and investor segments.

Fundraising for EQT XI and EQT Infrastructure VII progressed, with both funds expected to be activated in the coming months, while evergreen net inflows reached €0.9 billion and evergreen NAV €11 billion. AI Infrastructure assets climbed to a NAV of $11.5 billion, up more than 20% in the quarter, supported by $0.9 billion in net inflows and $1.2 billion of value development, highlighting strong investor appetite for technology and data-related infrastructure.

Learn more about TipRanks Premium Over the last twelve months, EQT announced gross fund investments of €30 billion, almost doubling the prior-year volume, and gross fund exits and co-invest realizations of €29 billion, reflecting high levels of deployment and realizations across private capital and infrastructure strategies. Deal activity included the conclusion of the investment period for EQT X, a new power and AI infrastructure investment by EQT Infrastructure VII, seven thematic investments for the Scaleup Europe Fund, and partial exits from U.S. logistics portfolios and mid-market strategies in Asia and Europe.

Operationally, all key funds continued to perform on or above plan and delivered 5% value creation during the quarter, supporting the growth in assets under management, with FAUM rising to €195 billion and total AUM to €354 billion at period end. The firm’s workforce expanded to 2,274 full-time employees, and capital returns to shareholders over the last twelve months totaled €712 million through dividends and share repurchases, indicating continued shareholder-focused capital allocation alongside rapid platform expansion.

The most recent analyst rating on EQT +4.05% ▲ stock is a Buy with a SEK410.00 price target. To see the full list of analyst forecasts on EQT AB stock, see the SE:EQT Stock Forecast page.

EQT AB is a global private capital and infrastructure investment manager, active across private equity, real estate, secondaries and thematic funds. The firm focuses on long-term, active ownership and manages a broad platform of strategies, including evergreen vehicles and specialized funds targeting sectors such as AI infrastructure, logistics, healthcare and technology, with a growing presence in Asia and the Middle East.

Through its diversified portfolio and expanding geographic footprint, EQT aims to capture institutional and private wealth capital flows while deploying capital into high-growth and mission-critical assets. The group’s scale and product breadth position it as one of Europe’s leading alternative asset managers, with significant fee-generating assets under management and a strong pipeline of investments and exits.

EQT’s business model relies on fundraising for successive flagship funds, performance-driven fee income and value creation in portfolio companies. Recent strategic moves, including acquisitions and platform launches, underscore its efforts to broaden capabilities in secondaries, real estate and evergreen solutions, enhancing its competitiveness in the global alternatives market.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) TSM -3.40% ▼ reported record third-quarter earnings on Thursday, October 15, as demand for AI chips remained strong. Net income rose 68.7% year over year to NT$763.06 billion ($23.59 billion), beating analyst estimates. Revenue also reached a record NT$1.494 trillion.

For context,TSMC is the world’s largest contract chipmaker. The company supplies advanced semiconductors to top tech giants, including AppleAAPL +0.50% ▲ and NvidiaNVDA -3.16% ▼.

TSMC’s revenue climbed 50.9% year over year to NT$1.494 trillion. In U.S. dollar terms, revenue reached $46.72 billion, up 41.2% from a year earlier and 16.2% from the previous quarter. The result topped analyst expectations by $1.02 billion. Net income also rose 8% from Q2.

Technology investors who refuse to pick growth or income now have TDAQ.

Diluted earnings per share reached NT$29.43, equal to $4.60 per American depositary receipt (ADR). Both net income and diluted EPS increased 68.7% from a year earlier.

Gross margin came in at 66.4%, down from 67.7% in Q2. Operating margin fell to 58.7% from 60.3%. Net profit margin stood at 51.1%. Even with the quarter-over-quarter declines, TSMC reported strong profit growth.

The company also gave a positive outlook for the next quarter. It expects Q4 revenue to reach $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, which would mark a further increase from Q3.

Advanced chip production remained a major source of sales. Technologies at 7nm and below accounted for 79% of wafer revenue in Q3, up from 77% in Q2. The 3nm process contributed 33%, followed by 5nm at 28%. The 7nm and 2nm processes accounted for 10% and 8%, respectively.

These processes help make chips faster and more power-efficient. They are used in advanced processors for AI and other demanding computing tasks. The high share of wafer revenue from these technologies shows the role they play in TSMC’s business.

To meet demand, TSMC plans to spend between $60 billion and $64 billion on capital projects in 2026. The investment will help the company expand its production capacity, though it also requires large sums for factories and equipment.

TSMC shares fell 3.4% to $430 in U.S. trading on October 14. The stock then dropped to $422.55 in after-hours trading, down a further 1.73%.

The decline came as AI stocks faced a broad sell-off. Hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data raised concerns about borrowing costs. Investors were also wary of the high cost of expanding AI infrastructure.

Despite the recent dip, TSMC stock has gained more than 42% so far this year, driven by strong demand for AI chips.

According to TipRanks,TSM stockhas a Strong Buy consensus rating based on seven Buys and one Hold assigned in the last three months. At $553.00,TSMC’s average stock price targetimplies a 29% upside potential.
